beats.narration_en: Why would road crews park a truck right in your lane?
It's a shield, parked on purpose between traffic and the workers.
On its back is a crash cushion that folds down like a tail.
Inside are blocks of thin aluminum honeycomb.
When a car hits, the honeycomb crushes row by row.
So the car slows down over about eight feet of crushing metal.
The truck is heavy and braked, so it only rolls a few feet.
It's built to stop a five-thousand-pound pickup at sixty-two miles an hour.
In one state, drivers hit thirty-nine of them in under eight months.
